## The Core Problem Solved
Statistical language models (LLMs) hallucinate by sounding completely convincing. They smooth over missing evidence, strip conditional qualifiers, substitute different questions, and claim authority they do not possess.
Standard semantic guardrails (toxicity filters, regex, sentiment analysis) only check for offensive words or jailbreaks—they cannot evaluate whether evidence actually warrants a consequential action.

WHP Decision Integrity evaluates whether an agent's claim and requested operation (moving money, merging code, filing compliance) are structurally and evidentially warranted by the submitted authority and provenance, enforcing Invariant I.1: Action Force cannot exceed Premise Support (A(c) <= P(c)).

## The Four Named Failures Detected & Halted
1. Coherent Substitution: Answering a materially different proposition while presenting the output as responsive to the original.
2. Authority Leakage: Converting descriptive informational findings into consequential execution authority without an admitted warrant.
3. Qualifier Stripping: Dropping temporal, situational, or environmental caveats when propagating conclusions.
4. Object Drift: Subtly altering the identity or boundary of the governed entity across inference steps.

## Cryptographic Standing Mark
Every determination is canonicalized (RFC 8785) and cryptographically signed with WHP's authoritative Ed25519 issuer key. The signed mark is portable, self-contained, and independently verifiable offline or via /v1/verification.
